title: A worker's session can start real paid claude sessions: nothing in its environment stops a smoke test from calling claude
goal: dispatch starts the worker's own session by the absolute path of the claude it found and gives the session a PATH whose first directory holds a stub claude that exits 2 naming the item and the spend gate it needs, unless the item carries an answered gate that names money (bl_authority's strict money signal), when the PATH is unchanged, so a worker's child call of claude reaches the real binary only for an item whose spend the operator approved, in new, resumed and begun dispatches alike

run:
import glob, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    bindir = os.path.join(d, "bin"); os.mkdir(bindir)
    mark = os.path.join(d, "paid-call-made")
    open(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), "w").write(
        "#!/bin/sh\n"
        "case \"$*\" in\n"
        "  *--add-dir*) cat >/dev/null; claude -p smoke-test >/dev/null 2>&1; echo '{\"is_error\":false,\"session_id\":\"s\"}' ;;\n"
        "  *smoke-test*) echo called >> \"$PAID_MARK\" ;;\n"
        "esac\n")
    os.chmod(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), 0o755)
    env = dict(os.environ, PATH=bindir + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"], PAID_MARK=mark, KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(d, "coord.sqlite"))
    origin = os.path.join(d, "origin.git")
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", origin], check=True)
    root = os.path.join(d, "root"); os.mkdir(root)
    def g(*a):
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, *a], capture_output=True, text=True)
    def bl(*a):
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "--root", root, *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=120)
    g("init", "-q", "-b", "main"); g("config", "user.email", "x@example.com"); g("config", "user.name", "x"); g("remote", "add", "origin", origin)
    open(os.path.join(root, "README"), "w").write("x\n"); g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "init"); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main")
    iid = bl("new", "story", "--title", "T", "--goal", "g", "--touch", "f.txt", "--check", "python3 -c pass").stdout.split()[2]
    path = glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", iid + ".json"), recursive=True)[0]
    item = json.load(open(path)); item["status"] = "todo"; json.dump(item, open(path, "w"))
    g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "plant todo"); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main")
    claimed = bl("claim", iid, "--by", "claude-aaaaaaaa")
    assert claimed.returncode == 0, ("claim", (claimed.stdout + claimed.stderr)[-300:])
    dispatched = bl("dispatch", iid)
    assert dispatched.returncode == 0, ("dispatch", (dispatched.stdout + dispatched.stderr)[-300:])
    assert not os.path.exists(mark), "a worker with no approved spend gate started a real claude session"

notes: Retro finding of the drain: ST-i5az334d's worker started 4 real Haiku 5.5 sessions (about 0.011 USD) as a smoke test though only other items of the sprint had an approved spend; the brief's rule on spending is text only. Premise (reproduces: the repro): worker_env (bl_dispatch.py) passes the dispatching session's PATH, so a worker's child call of claude reaches the real binary whatever its item's gates say. The stub is the retro's first example; the other, a spend check at done, would find the spend only afterwards and is left to the planner. Popen resolves argv[0] with the PATH it is given, so the stub directory must go on the PATH only after dispatch has resolved the real claude to a path; worker_env is also called by bench_load.py: keep its signature compatible. The repro plants a fake claude as the dispatched binary and as its child's target (no model call). Related: ST-ybksk2f2 (the opposite rule: an item whose code starts claude -p proves one capped real call).
